newsitem.title: POLAND: OPTIMUS SEES 1997 NET PROFIT UP 80 PCT.
newsitem.headline: OPTIMUS SEES 1997 NET PROFIT UP 80 PCT.

text.p: Polish computer maker Optimus SA expects to lift net profit this year to 30 million zlotys from 16.5 million zlotys in 1996, the firm's financial director said on Tuesday.

"This year the net profit of Optimus is seen at 30 million zlotys, growth of about 80 percent," Stefan Mroczek told a news conference, adding that last year's sales of 501.1 million zlotys should increase by 30 to 40 percent.
He said the significant profit growth would be made possible by activities in high-margin, non-computer areas such as multimedia and telecommunication.

Mroczek said the firm's earnings-per-share would rise to 4.62 zlotys at the end of this year from the current 3.72 zlotys, assuming the conversion of all the firm's 300 convertible bonds at a par value of $100,000.

Earlier in the day Optimus said in a statement that 159 of the five-year bonds had been placed with financial investors from Asia and Europe. Earlier this month the firm received orders to convert the bonds into 6,947 shares each.
Mroczek said the firm would use its call option on the bonds sometime in this year's first half if it had not already received orders to convert them.
He said 1997 group eps would be at 6.67 zlotys, assuming a 15-million-zloty 1997 net profit by cash-register subsidiary Optimus IC, of which Optimus SA holds 88.3 percent.

Mroczek said the firm's 33-percent January net-profit rise to about 1.2 million zlotys was gained on sales down to 23.7 million zlotys from about 40 million, as the firm was slowed that month due to the introduction of a new computer system.
